name: mxgmn/WaveFunctionCollapse
description: The original Wave Function Collapse algorithm generating bitmap and tilemap output from a single example image, drawing on ideas from quantum mechanics. Widely used in commercial games including Bad North, Caves of Qud, and Townscaper; ported to every major language and engine.
score_rationale: The canonical WFC implementation with massive community adoption and ports to C++, Rust, Unity, Godot, and Unreal.

name: mxgmn/MarkovJunior
description: A probabilistic language based on pattern matching and constraint propagation that unifies constructive and constraint-based procedural generation with 153 included examples. Generates everything from mazes to voxel scenes entirely through rewrite rules.
score_rationale: Highly original system from the WFC author pushing the state of the art in grid-based procedural generation with broad academic and game-dev interest.

name: BorisTheBrave/DeBroglie
description: A C# library implementing Wave Function Collapse with full backtracking support, additional non-local constraints, and NuGet distribution for easy integration. Designed for production use in game pipelines where vanilla WFC would fail to resolve contradictions.
score_rationale: The most production-ready WFC library for .NET/Unity with constraint extensions and active documentation that vanilla WFC lacks.

name: Auburn/FastNoiseLite
description: An extremely portable noise generation library supporting Perlin, Simplex, Value, Cellular, and Domain Warp noise across C#, C++, C, Java, HLSL, GLSL, JavaScript, Rust, and Go from a single header or file. Designed for real-time terrain and texture generation.
score_rationale: The dominant portable noise library with multi-language support and widespread adoption across game engines and graphics pipelines.

name: KdotJPG/OpenSimplex2
description: Patent-free successors to OpenSimplex noise providing visually isotropic coherent noise in 2D, 3D, and 4D with implementations in Java, C#, C++, Python, and GLSL. Created to replace Simplex noise without IP concerns.
score_rationale: The authoritative patent-free alternative to Simplex noise with multi-language implementations from the original OpenSimplex author.

name: Auburn/FastNoiseSIMD
description: A C++ noise library accelerated with SIMD CPU intrinsics (SSE2 through AVX512) achieving up to 700% speed improvements over scalar implementations for Perlin, Simplex, Cellular, and Value noise. Intended for high-performance terrain and texture generation at runtime.
score_rationale: Best-in-class performance noise library for CPU-bound generation pipelines using SIMD vectorization.

name: Jaysmito101/TerraForge3D
description: A cross-platform procedural terrain generation and texturing tool featuring a node editor with 40+ nodes, hydraulic and wind erosion algorithms, and GLSL shader export. Fully free and open-source as a standalone application.
score_rationale: Feature-rich standalone terrain tool rivaling commercial products, with node-based editing and multiple erosion simulations.

name: SebLague/Procedural-Planets
description: A Unity-based procedural planet generator using layered noise functions, LOD spherical mesh generation, and biome-based surface coloring. Companion to a popular educational YouTube series on procedural generation techniques.
score_rationale: Highly educational Unity reference implementation with thousands of learners and clear pedagogical code structure.

name: Hoimar/Planet-Generator
description: A procedural planet generator Godot addon using layered noise with dynamic terrain LOD and chunk streaming, written in GDScript. Drop-in plugin for Godot 3 projects needing spherical world generation.
score_rationale: The primary Godot-native procedural planet plugin with LOD support and clean addon architecture.

name: audinowho/RogueElements
description: A game-agnostic roguelike map generation library using a modular pipeline of GenSteps, supporting room placement, BSP splitting, mazes, corridors, and content population. Designed to be engine-independent and fully customizable.
score_rationale: The most complete game-agnostic roguelike map generation library with a composable pipeline architecture.

name: tlhunter/node-roguelike
description: A Node.js library for generating top-down 2D dungeon maps using BSP trees, room placement, and corridor carving with configurable parameters. Lightweight npm package for JavaScript roguelike and dungeon-crawler games.
score_rationale: Clean, dependency-free JavaScript dungeon generation library suitable for browser and server-side game projects.

name: shun126/DungeonGenerator
description: A procedural 3D dungeon generator Unreal Engine 5 plugin that creates levels, mini-maps, and mission graphs for roguelike games. Supports runtime generation with Blueprint integration and automatic room connectivity.
score_rationale: The leading open-source UE5 dungeon generation plugin with mission graph support and Blueprint-friendly API.

name: Adrian104/Dungeon-Generator
description: A seed-driven BSP-based procedural 2D dungeon map generator producing deterministic, reproducible layouts with configurable room count and corridor style. Lightweight and engine-agnostic.
score_rationale: Well-structured BSP dungeon generator with deterministic seed support making it easy to reproduce and share layouts.

name: t-mw/citygen
description: An interactive procedural city generation demo using road network growth algorithms inspired by the 2001 Parish & Muller paper, rendered in the browser. Generates organic and grid street layouts with building footprints.
score_rationale: One of the most faithful open-source implementations of the seminal Parish-Muller city generation algorithm, usable in the browser.

name: tudelft3d/Random3Dcity
description: A procedural modelling engine from TU Delft generating CityGML buildings and urban features at multiple levels of detail for research and benchmarking. Produces standards-compliant synthetic city datasets.
score_rationale: Unique academic tool producing standards-compliant CityGML synthetic data for GIS and urban simulation research.

name: openalea/lpy
description: An open-source Python implementation of Lindenmayer Systems for modeling plant growth and morphogenesis, mixing L-system construction with Python scripting. Used in botany research and 3D virtual plant simulation.
score_rationale: The primary scientific L-system toolkit with active botanical research community and full Python integration.

name: openalea/plantgl
description: An open-source C++/Python graphic toolkit for the creation, simulation, and analysis of 3D virtual plants, providing geometric primitives, L-system integration, and visualization tools. Foundation of the OpenAlea plant modeling platform.
score_rationale: Comprehensive 3D plant modeling library combining geometry, simulation, and visualization used in plant science research.

name: tsahyt/surfacelab
description: A node-based procedural texture generation application written in Rust, providing a graph editor for composing noise, filters, and blending operations into tileable surface materials. Targets artists and game asset pipelines.
score_rationale: Ambitious Rust-native procedural texture tool with node graph UI addressing the gap between Substance Designer and open-source tooling.

name: manankarnik/bevy_generative
description: A Bevy engine plugin for real-time procedural generation of maps, textures, terrain, and planets using noise and configurable parameters. Provides a unified API for multiple generation types within the Bevy ECS framework.
score_rationale: The primary procedural generation plugin for the rapidly growing Bevy ecosystem covering terrain, planets, and textures in one package.

name: gdquest-demos/godot-procedural-generation
description: A collection of procedural generation algorithms and playable demos for the Godot game engine covering WFC, maze generation, and terrain techniques. Published by GDQuest as an educational open-source reference.
score_rationale: Well-maintained educational repository from a leading Godot education platform covering multiple PCG algorithms with runnable demos.

name: RayTracing/raytracing.github.io
description: Official home of the 'Ray Tracing in One Weekend' book series with full C++ source code and free online books covering path tracing fundamentals. The de-facto educational starting point for anyone learning ray tracing.
score_rationale: Industry-standard educational resource for ray tracing with 10k+ stars, widely referenced in academia and industry, actively maintained.

name: mmp/pbrt-v3
description: Source code for pbrt, the renderer described in the third edition of 'Physically Based Rendering: From Theory To Implementation'. Companion code to the most widely read PBR textbook with 5k+ stars.
score_rationale: Widely studied reference renderer accompanying the landmark PBR textbook, with 5k stars and extensive community adoption.

name: EmbarkStudios/kajiya
description: Experimental real-time global illumination renderer built with Rust and Vulkan, implementing techniques like ReSTIR GI and IRCACHE. Showcases modern GI approaches from a game studio, though no longer maintained.
score_rationale: 5.3k-star real-time GI renderer from a game studio using cutting-edge techniques; valuable reference despite being abandoned.

name: nvpro-samples/vk_raytracing_tutorial_KHR
description: Official NVIDIA ray tracing tutorial and examples using the VK_KHR_ray_tracing Vulkan extension, covering 18+ progressive tutorials from basic setup to advanced techniques like motion blur and shader execution reorder.
score_rationale: Official NVIDIA Vulkan ray tracing tutorial with 1.7k stars; authoritative learning resource for production Vulkan RT development.

name: knightcrawler25/GLSL-PathTracer
description: Toy physically based GPU path tracer running in GLSL fragment shaders (C++/OpenGL), featuring Disney BSDF, multiple light types, image-based lighting, and importance sampling. Popular teaching and experimentation platform.
score_rationale: 2k-star GPU path tracer accessible via GLSL/OpenGL without requiring RTX hardware, popular for learning PBR techniques.

name: erichlof/THREE.js-PathTracing-Renderer
description: Real-time path tracing with global illumination and progressive rendering running entirely in the browser via Three.js and WebGL, achieving 30-60 FPS on consumer hardware. Extensive collection of interactive demos.
score_rationale: 2.2k-star browser-based path tracer that makes ray tracing accessible without native code, with rich demo library and active maintenance.

name: RenderKit/ospray
description: Intel OSPRay: an open, scalable, portable ray tracing engine for high-fidelity scientific visualization supporting x86, ARM, and Intel GPU via SYCL. Powers visualization tools across HPC and scientific applications.
score_rationale: Intel-backed production renderer with 1.1k stars, widely used in HPC/scientific visualization, actively maintained with GPU support.

name: GPSnoopy/RayTracingInVulkan
description: Implementation of Peter Shirley's Ray Tracing in One Weekend using Vulkan VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline, achieving ~140fps at 1280x720 on an RTX 2080 Ti. Practical reference for RTX hardware ray tracing.
score_rationale: 1.5k-star implementation bridging the popular RTIOW book with real Vulkan RTX hardware, actively updated through 2025.

name: gkjohnson/three-gpu-pathtracer
description: GPU-accelerated path tracing renderer and utilities for three.js built on three-mesh-bvh, supporting physically-based GGX materials, skinned meshes, area lights, volumes, and depth of field in WebGL 2.
score_rationale: 1.7k-star actively maintained WebGL path tracer for three.js with broad feature coverage and production-quality output.

name: NVIDIA-RTX/RTXPT
description: NVIDIA's production real-time path tracing library and sample integrating DLSS, RTXDI, and denoising, intended as a clean starting point for game engine path tracer integration. Supports DirectX 12 and Vulkan.
score_rationale: Official NVIDIA production path tracing reference with 917 stars, actively maintained through 2026 with cutting-edge RT techniques.
